questions.question: A byte-splitting or vocab-longest-match tokenizer that never consults the merge table can satisfy round-trip (AC-TOK-2), special-token handling (AC-TOK-3), and even the mutated-fixture behavioral check (AC-DEP-1, since renaming a vocab entry or reordering merge ranks can be observed without ever applying a merge) — AC-TOK-7's exact tokenId-sequence match is the only real discriminator. Demonstrate that AC-TOK-7's test would fail for a merge-table-free implementation: reason precisely from the vocab fixture what a byte-level/no-merge split of "strawberry" would produce as tokenIds (one element per byte or per single-character vocab entry, i.e. far more than 3), and show this differs from the golden fixture's 3-token entry for "strawberry" (per the terminology glossary). Do not accept an implementation whose AC-TOK-7 test still passes with merge-application short-circuited or no-op'd — if such a no-op run were performed, the test must fail visibly.

answer.evidence: AC-TOK-7 golden loop discriminates merge-table-free implementations: byte-split 'strawberry' yields 10 tokenIds vs golden 3. tokenizer.test.ts:207-211.
answer.answered_by: base:verification-examiner (4 parallel batches); VQ-S3-008 rescored by the lead after Decider adjudication

questions.question: decodeTokens() in server/tokenizer.ts decodes token bytes through ONE streaming TextDecoder (stream:true) per tokenize() call, with ignoreBOM:true, specifically to guarantee tokens.join("") === s even when a BPE boundary falls mid-character or the input starts with U+FEFF. Confirm a test exists that would fail if this streaming/ignoreBOM design were reverted to a naive per-token new TextDecoder().decode(bytes) call (no stream flag, default ignoreBOM) — see tests/integration/tokenizer.test.ts's "leading BOM" and general AC-TOK-6 property tests. This resolves ownership-ledger.json's carried-forward S2-F4 finding (formatTokenViewText indexes by UTF-16 code unit; a byte-level BPE boundary mid-character could otherwise insert a separator inside a character) at the tokenizer layer rather than the formatter layer: tokens returned by tokenize() are now guaranteed to be complete, valid substrings of the input, so token-view.ts's existing UTF-16-offset-based formatter needed no change.

answer.evidence: decodeTokens uses ONE streaming TextDecoder('utf-8',{ignoreBOM:true}) per tokenize() call with stream:true, so tokens.join('')===s holds across BPE boundaries that split a multi-byte character. Leading-BOM case explicitly tested. Downstream lossiness (a zero-length token's boundary collapsing into its neighbour's offset in the Set) is documented and pinned by a formatter test.
answer.answered_by: base:verification-examiner (4 parallel batches); VQ-S3-008 rescored by the lead after Decider adjudication
